questions.question: A number chain starts at 250, and every new number is 250 more than the one before it. The chain so far is 250, 500, 750. What number comes next in the chain?
questions.explain: Skip-counting by 250 four times gives 250, 500, 750, 1000 — four 250s make one thousand. The trap is losing or gaining a zero: 1000 is not 100 and not 10 000.

questions.question: Marisol counts forward by 25 000 out loud. She says 25 000, then 50 000, then 75 000. What is the very next number she says?
questions.explain: Four jumps of 25 000 land on 100 000, so 75 000 + 25 000 = 100 000 (one hundred thousand). Watch the placeholder zeros — 10 000 has one zero too few and 1 000 000 has too many.

questions.question: A counting chain goes backward by 500 each time, starting at 3000. The chain so far is 3000, 2500, 2000. What number comes next?
questions.explain: Counting back by 500 takes away five hundreds, so 2000 - 500 = 1500. The common slip is changing only the tens (2000 to 1950) or writing the answer with the wrong number of zeros.

questions.question: A number line has marks spaced exactly 1000 apart. The first three marks are labelled 4005, 5005 and 6005. The fourth mark is blank. What number belongs on the blank mark?
questions.explain: Adding 1000 changes only the thousands digit, so 6005 becomes 7005 and the 0 and 5 stay put. The big trap is moving or dropping the placeholder zero, which turns 7005 into 705 or 70 005.

questions.question: A forestry group near Prince George plants 25 000 seedlings every spring. They have planted 75 000 seedlings so far. How many will they have planted after two more springs?
questions.explain: Skip-count on by 25 000 twice: 75 000, 100 000, 125 000. Stopping after one jump gives 100 000, and miscounting the zeros gives 12 500 or 1 250 000.

questions.question: Which list of numbers is a correct skip-count forward by 250?
questions.explain: Each jump of 250 adds two hundreds and a fifty, so 1750 + 250 = 2000. The list that jumps by 50 is too small, and the ones ending in 200 or 20 000 lost or gained a placeholder zero.

questions.question: Ben skip-counts backward by 1000 starting at 102 000. What number does he say on his third jump back?
questions.explain: Count back 102 000, 101 000, 100 000, 99 000 — the third jump crosses below one hundred thousand. Stopping at 100 000 is one jump short, and 9900 or 990 000 has the wrong number of zeros.

questions.question: Marcus wants to count from 3000 up to 5000 using exactly 4 equal jumps. Which skip-count should he use?
questions.explain: The gap is 2000, and 4 equal jumps means each one is 500: 3000, 3500, 4000, 4500, 5000. Counting by 250 takes 8 jumps, while 50 and 5000 are the same digits with the zeros mismatched.

questions.question: A trail crew on Vancouver Island lays 250 m of gravel each work day. They have already laid 1500 m and the finished trail must be 3500 m long. After 6 more work days, how many more metres will still be needed?
questions.explain: Skip-count 250 six times to get 1500 m, add it to the 1500 m already laid for 3000 m, then 3500 - 3000 = 500 m left. Counting only 5 days leaves 750 m, and mixing up the zeros turns 500 into 50 or 5000.

questions.question: A Surrey school wants to raise $10 000 for new bikes. They have $4000 so far, and every spirit day raises exactly $1000 more. How many more spirit days do they need?
questions.explain: Skip-count by 1000 from 4000 up to 10 000: 5000, 6000, 7000, 8000, 9000, 10 000 — that is 6 days. Counting from $0 instead of $4000 gives 10 days, and an extra zero turns 6 into 60.

questions.question: Jasmin skip-counts forward by 25 000 starting at 175 000. She says 175 000, then 200 000, then 225 000, then 25 000. What should the last number have been, and why?
options: She should have said 205 000, because the extra zero goes right after the 2.
She should have said 2 500 000, because counting on opens a new place.
She should have said 250 000, because 225 000 plus 25 000 makes 250 000.
She should have said 225 025, because 25 000 changes only the end digits.
questions.explain: Adding 25 000 to 225 000 gives 250 000 — two hundred fifty thousand. Jasmin said the jump size instead of the total, which is the same slip as dropping placeholder zeros from a big number.

questions.question: Amrit and Priya both start their counting at 12 000. Amrit counts on by 1000 five times. Priya counts on by 500 eight times. Who ends on the larger number, and by how much?
questions.explain: Amrit adds 5000 to reach 17 000 and Priya adds 4000 to reach 16 000, so Amrit is ahead by 1000. The trap is on the difference: 17 000 - 16 000 is 1000, not 100 or 10 000.
